annotations.title: Correct rows of a declared format

description: Change columns of rows already stored — **a list of edits in one call**. Each names its row by `id` or by `where` (`{ref: "INV-0042"}`, which survives another writer; a text document renews ids on every write), and the `values` to change. `expect` (`{state: "planned"}`) refuses the batch unless the row still holds that, so two sessions cannot both take one row. Every column not named is left exactly as it was, which is the difference between this and the app: `#/formats/<name>` shows a person every column and writes every column, and this corrects three of thirty across a batch. A required column cannot be emptied. A `link` value may be the name of the row it points at, or a unique column of it (`course: {notion_id: "a1b2"}`), as in `record_format_rows`. Returns the before-and-after and writes nothing until `commit: true`.

commit.description: Write it. Omit or false for the dry run.

edits.description: One entry per row. Up to 200 in a call.

expect.description: Values the row must still hold.

id.description: The row’s id, as `format_rows` printed it. Or `where`.

values.description: Column name to its new value. Columns left out do not change.

where.description: Instead of `id`: values naming exactly one row.

path.description: Absolute path to a .emd file on this machine.
